2006 Volvo XC90 pricing starts at $2,900 for the XC90 2.5T Sport Utility 4D, which had a starting MSRP of $38,110 when new. The range-topping 2006 XC90 V8 Ocean Race Ed Sport Utility 4D starts at $3,525 today, originally priced from $50,555.

The prices here reflect what buyers are currently paying for used 2006 Volvo XC90 models in typical condition when purchasing from a dealership. These prices are updated weekly.


XC90 Consumer Sentiment

Owners give this generation Volvo XC90 (2003-2014) a 4.1 out of 5 rating, which is higher than most, and 73% recommend it. These figures are based on 485 consumer reviews, like these:

What Owners are Saying About the 2006 Volvo XC90

"The Epitome of a Volvo"

"In 2003, my family made the best decision of our lives. We bought our silver XC90 brand new and will never get rid of it. In the 17 years that we have owned this fantastic piece of machinery, it has needed no major repairs. The interior could definitely use some work, but this has been our workhorse of a vehicle: school drop off, hauling, moving, you name it. This tank truly showcases Volvo's superior safety and reliability, where some people only get rid of theirs because they get bored with their model. I think the only "major" thing we needed to do was change the timing belt at 110k. Yes, we only have about 152k miles and it's been with us for almost 20 years, but it still has the same power and fierceness it did in its first year. Heck, we love this car so much, we bought a 2nd one, a 2018 Inscription! Youngest is taking it as a commuter to college for the next few years. If you ever come across one, a 5 cylinder only, avoid the original T6 until around the 2008 "facelift" version, we highly recommend you check it out and buy one for yourself :)"

"Amazing in Snow"

"Buy this Vehicle for your family's safety if you live in the snow or ice. Three blizzards in Colorado, towed our Volvo S60 R to California over 14,000 foot Rockies, after 81,000 miles the car is still going strong. Buy the extended warrentee: many repairs needed cost only $100 per deductable. Two engine mounts, propeller shaft (drive shaft), new rack & Pinion Steering. Gyroscope under driver's seat is amazing and the STC sensors on the wheels. The result: it is impossible to put this car into a skid in snow. . . believe me I tried. The antio skid system puts the right amount of braking and reduced the engine power to straighten out the car! During one of the three Blizzards of 2006/2007 we passed dozens of stranded cars, trucks, and even a police officer stuck at an intersection. Get studless snow tires with ground up Walnut Shells (Blizex) and it stops even on black ice! Amazing. Now we live in California and enjoy sun every day and our 7 month old has plenty of room for her car seat and baby equipment. Bottom line: great car, some repairs needed, but I was surprised to see all of the people's complaints about repairs -- just like humans cars need a little investment. I will go with a Volvo again."

"Volvo never disappoints!"

"Safest tank I've ever driven. Solid. Dependable SUV. Plush ride. Newer Michelin tires. Ignition coils and fuel injectors recently replaced. Regular service through reputable mechanic. He suggests radiator needs to be replaced soon. Apparently the 2005 and 2006 FWD are bulletproof."

Overall 2006 Volvo XC90 Quality

User sentiment suggests the overall quality of the 2006 Volvo XC90 is above average for its class. Owners rated the 2006 Volvo XC90 quality a 4.2 out of 5.

2006 Volvo XC90 Reliability

The 2006 Volvo XC90 receives an average consumer rating of 4.1 overall and a 4.2 for reliability, which means owners consider its reliability to be above average.

2006 Volvo XC90 V8

The 2006 Volvo XC90 is a midsize luxury SUV known for its safety features, practicality, and Scandinavian design aesthetic. It marked an important milestone as one of the first SUVs to prioritize safety with a strong emphasis on passenger protection. The XC90's interior is comfortable and spacious, offering seating for up to seven passengers across three rows. The materials used are of high quality, and the build quality is solid, reflecting Volvo's commitment to safety and craftsmanship. It has a comprehensive safety suite, which includes standard features like stability control, side-curtain airbags, and Volvo's Roll Stability Control. It also introduced Volvo's innovative "Integrated Booster Cushion" for child safety. Overall, the 2006 Volvo XC90 is a safe and practical choice for families in need of a midsize SUV with premium features.

Anonymous

Reviewed a 2005 Volvo 2.5T Turbo FWD on Dec 13, 2011

6cd changer, power seats, 2.5l turbocharged engine, and a lot of safety features make this a great family car. If need to load, huge cargo area by folding third row, second row, and even passenger side front seat. Incredible sound system, really stable suv

Is this review helpful?

Victor B

Reviewed a 2005 Volvo 2.5T Turbo FWD on Aug 5, 2009

If you value performance, then this is not the car for you. The 2.5T is a small engine for something so big, so performance is nothing to write home about. It was not designed to be a performance car. 0-60 mph takes 11 seconds or so. Around corners, it rolls heavily and throttle will result in serious understeer. The steering is as vague as it gets. The first half an inch or so of steering in either direction from center does nothing at all. However, if performance is not your top priority, then this is an excellent car in terms of practicality and comfort. The ride is quite soft. The seats are fairly comfortable. There isn't too much road or tire noise. It can seat 7 people, though the two seats in the very back have little legroom. Those are best left for the children. With the seats folded down, there is plenty of room for cargo, enough for something like a small couch. The split tailgate is a nice touch and makes loading heavy items easier.

@graph.name: 2005 Volvo XC90 2.5T Turbo FWD

review.reviewBody: 6cd changer, power seats, 2.5l turbocharged engine, and a lot of safety features make this a great family car.  If need to load, huge cargo area by folding third row, second row, and even passenger side front seat.   Incredible sound system, really stable suv

If you value performance, then this is not the car for you. The 2.5T is a small engine for something so big, so performance is nothing to write home about. It was not designed to be a performance car. 0-60 mph takes 11 seconds or so. Around corners, it rolls heavily and throttle will result in serious understeer. The steering is as vague as it gets. The first half an inch or so of steering in either direction from center does nothing at all.

However, if performance is not your top priority, then this is an excellent car in terms of practicality and comfort. The ride is quite soft. The seats are fairly comfortable. There isn't too much road or tire noise. It can seat 7 people, though the two seats in the very back have little legroom. Those are best left for the children. With the seats folded down, there is plenty of room for cargo, enough for something like a small couch. The split tailgate is a nice touch and makes loading heavy items easier.
